a_chain.why: Step 7b: [Mon] [Tue] [Wed-Sun], four ranks on a Monday in a gap of Monday and Tuesday, three on a Tuesday in a gap of Tuesday and Wednesday; Monday two over and the last group two under, which no Monday rank's gap holds.

a_chain_in_order.why: Step 7b's search, one group a weekday: Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday are each over and Friday one under; the Monday's gap reaches the Tuesday, the first Tuesday's and the Wednesday's reach the Friday, and a second Tuesday's reaches the Friday after. a_chain_in_the_pass.why: Step 7b through the whole pass, a unit of an hour with the day kept: a gap from Tuesday 12:00 to Wednesday 12:00, the census [00-11] [12-17] [18-23] owing one rank fewer in the first group and one more in the last. a_cycle_undone.why: Step 8.3's cycle undone, a day of moments, the count one short: a gap from Friday 20:00:00 to Monday 06:00:00 holds Saturday 10:00:00 twice and Sunday 10:00:00, and a gap of the week after next a lone Wednesday 12:00:00. a_day_freed_for_a_cycle.why: A day step 6 empties is free to step 8.3, a day of moments, each weekday its own group, the count two short: a gap from Monday to Saturday holds Tuesday 08:34:25 and Thursday 07:08:34 twice, and the gap after it the Tuesday after next; the census asks a Friday, and step 6 moves the first Tuesday's moment there. a_long_pair.why: Step 8.5: two cells of two weeks, a lone Saturday beside a Monday held twice, and a Tuesday held twice beside a Saturday held once; the count is one long.

a_long_pair_by_first_places.why: Step 8.5 measures two gaps apart from their first places, the count one long: a gap of one week, Sunday to Sunday, holds a Tuesday twice and a lone Saturday, between gaps of two weeks that each hold a Monday and a Saturday twice. The gap after it starts a week from its first place and the gap before it two weeks, though the one before ends a week from its last place and the one after two weeks: the Saturday joins the Tuesday and a Monday rank of the gap after takes its Saturday.

a_long_pair_by_two_first.why: Step 8.5 on a unit of an hour, minutes written, the day kept, the count two long: a gap from Tuesday 00:00 to Wednesday 23:00 holds 09:00 alone and 14:00 twice on the Tuesday and 08:00 alone and 15:00 twice on the Wednesday -- two cells with one first place -- and the gap after it 07:00 and 16:00 alone on the Friday. The Tuesday's 09:00 with a Wednesday 15:00 rank would take the count down by one, its two gaps no distance apart; with the Friday's lone 16:00 by two, and that pair is taken.

a_long_pair_in_the_pass.why: Step 8.5 through the whole pass, the census held and the count one long: a gap of a Friday held twice and a lone Saturday, and one of a Saturday and a Monday held twice each. No held day of its own group stands in either gap, so the lone Saturday joins the Friday and a Monday rank the other gap's Saturday.

a_long_pair_one_long.why: Step 8.5 with the count one long: the first gap holds a lone Saturday, a Monday held twice that is a hole and a Tuesday held twice; the second a Monday held once, a Wednesday held twice and a lone Saturday. The Saturday joins the Tuesday, not the hole, and a Wednesday rank joins the second gap's Saturday: the count falls by one, not two.

a_moments_day.why: A unit of a day of moments, seconds written: thirty weekday moments over two weeks, the census asking eight on the weekend; every move keeps the clock.

a_moments_run.why: Step 5 on a day of moments: two moments on Wednesday at 10:00:00 run together, and the census moves two weekday ranks to the weekend. The Sunday before and the Saturday after stand three days away, 10:00:00 free on both, a rank on the Sunday's midnight: the run goes whole to the Sunday at 10:00:00.

a_trade.why: Step 8.6, the second census the half of the month: Saturday the 16th is one over the weekend's total and reaches only Friday the 15th, in the other half, so Monday the 11th crosses the 15th the other way.

a_trade_back_31.why: Step 8.6's second move reaches 31 units: Saturday 16 March must go to the weekdays and reaches only Friday the 15th, in the first half of the month, so a weekday rank of the first half crosses back: Friday 1 March, every weekday of the second half within 30 days below it a hole, goes to Tuesday 30 January, 31 days below.

a_trade_in_the_pass.why: Step 8.6 through the whole pass, the second census the half of the month: Saturday the 16th must go to the weekdays and reaches only Friday the 15th, held, in the other half, so Thursday the 14th crosses to Monday the 18th, and the count falls by one; steps 8.1 to 8.5 then run again, and one of the two ranks on Tuesday the 5th goes to Wednesday the 6th.

a_trade_of_hours.why: Step 8.6 on a unit of an hour, the day kept: a rank at 01:00, its census group [00-07] one over and [16-23] one under, its gap from 20:00 the evening before; [08-15] holds its total. 23:00 the evening before is another day, and 08:00 a group at its total: the rank goes to 16:00.

a_trade_reaching_62.why: Step 8.6's reach of 62 units: 30 May 2024 must go to a 31st, 31 May is a hole, and 31 July stands 62 days on.

an_hour_inside_its_day.why: A unit of an hour, minutes written, the day kept: forty-two moments over three days, 01:00 to 05:59 and 13:00 to 16:59, and a census of hours [00-11] [12-23] asking ten more in the afternoon, which an early rank reaches sooner on the evening before.

an_hour_run.why: Step 5 on a unit of an hour, minutes written, the day kept: two ranks at 10:30 run together and the census of hours [00-11] [12-23] asks two more in the afternoon. A rank stands at 12:00 and 12:30 is free, so the run goes whole to 12:30.

every_cycle_of_seven.why: Step 8.3's cycles on seven groups, one weekday each: two ranks on a Monday, a Tuesday, a Wednesday and a Thursday of four weeks, each cell reaching the next weekday and Thursday's the Monday after, so only the cycle through the four gains.

long_pairs_count_the_pinned_rank.why: Step 8.5 counts every rank of the column on a unit, the count one long: the first gap's Sunday is held by a rank of the gap and by the pinned rank the gap starts at, beside a Monday held twice and a lone Saturday; the second gap holds a Tuesday and a Saturday twice each. The Sunday is not alone, so the lone Saturday joins the Monday and a Tuesday rank the second gap's Saturday.

long_pairs_leave_an_emptied_unit.why: Step 8.5 leaves a unit it empties: three gaps of two weeks, the count two long; the first holds a Monday twice and a lone Saturday, the second a Wednesday and a Saturday twice each, the third a Monday twice and a lone Saturday. The first gap's Saturday pairs with the second gap; then the first gap holds no weekend day, the third gap's Saturday has nowhere to pair, and the count stays one long.

long_pairs_move_a_joined_rank_again.why: Step 8.5 twice, the count two long, two gaps of two weeks: the first holds a lone Monday, a Saturday and a Tuesday held twice each, the second a Tuesday held twice, a lone Thursday and a Saturday held twice. The Monday rank joins its gap's Saturday and a second-gap Saturday rank joins its Tuesday; then the Thursday joins the Saturday left alone, and the first rank on the first gap's Saturday, the Monday rank that joined it, goes on to its Tuesday.

long_pairs_twice.why: Step 8.5 twice, the count two long, three gaps of two weeks: the first two hold a Monday and a Saturday twice each, the third a Monday twice and a lone Saturday and Sunday. The third gap's Saturday joins its Monday and pairs with the nearer gap, the second, whose Monday rank joins its Saturday; then that Monday, held once now, joins its Saturday too, and a first-gap Saturday rank joins its Monday.

merged_at_another_clock.why: Step 8.4: moments of one gap over three weeks, a Tuesday at 10:17:05 alone, weekdays at 14:00:00 held twice; the count is one long.

merged_at_its_clock.why: Step 8.4: moments of one gap over three weeks, a Tuesday at 10:17:05 alone, weekdays at 14:00:00 held twice, and 10:17:05 held a week later; the count is one long.

merged_in_a_second_round.why: Step 8.4's second round: three Mondays held once, once and three times, the third's gap reaching no other, the count two long. The first round merges the first onto the second; the second round merges those two onto the third.

merged_in_the_pass.why: Step 8.4 through the whole pass, a day of moments: Monday 09:00:00 and Tuesday 14:00:00 held twice each, and the census moving one to the weekend. The Monday rank goes to the Sunday before at 09:00:00, the count one long; no other moment stands at 09:00:00 on either group's days, so the Monday moment left alone joins Tuesday's 14:00:00.

merged_inside_the_shared_gap.why: Step 8.4's window, one group a weekday: two ranks on a Monday, one in a gap from the Sunday before it to five weeks on and one in a gap starting the Thursday after the Monday before; the Mondays a week either side are each held three times. the_index.why: Steps 5 and 6 on gaps long enough to be searched by index: two hundred weekday dates over forty weeks in three gaps, every twentieth from the third repeating the day before, the census asking fifty on the weekend.

the_index_reach.why: Steps 5 and 6's reach of 400 units through the index: 7 March 2024, in a gap from 30 January 2023, must go to a 31st; every 31st up to 400 days below it is a hole, and the one free 31st, 31 January 2023, stands 401 days below, so no move is offered.

the_prior_of_hours.why: Step 3's prior on a unit of an hour: a gap from Tuesday 06:00 to Friday 18:00, Tuesday and Thursday holes, the census [00-11] [12-23]. Every hour of a hole's day is a hole, the gap's first hour at half, so Wednesday's hours and Friday's to 18:00 alone count.

three_group_cycles_of_ten.why: Step 8.3's cycles on ten groups of the days of the month, the first nine days one group each and the 10th to the 31st the tenth: two ranks on 1 January, 2 February and 3 March 2024, each cell reaching the next group's day and the last 1 April, so only the cycle through the three gains.
